questions.question: A React component re-renders infinitely or a list shows stale data — walk through your debugging process.
questions.title: Debugging Frontend Scenarios
questions.direct_answer: Infinite re-render: an effect updates state it also reads — check the dependency array and whether the effect writes state unconditionally. Stale list: state mutation instead of replacement (same reference), or a stale closure capturing old values. Process: reproduce → isolate (comment out halves) → read the state flow (who writes, who reads, when) → fix the root cause (missing/wrong dep, mutated state, missing key) → add a guard (lint rules, logging render causes).

Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[symptom: infinite render OR stale UI] --> R{reproduce + bisect}
    R --> A{infinite?}
    A -->|yes| E[effect writes state it depends on]
    A -->|no| M{stale?}
    M -->|same ref| MU[state mutated — Object.is sees no change]
    M -->|child not updating| MEMO[memo child with changing props]
    M -->|wrong rows| K[key identity mismatch]
    E --> F1[derive with useMemo / fix deps]
    MU --> F2[new reference: spread, map, concat]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The render-trigger contract (the model that makes all these debuggable): React re-renders a component when (1) its own state changes — via a setter with a NEW reference/value, (2) its parent re-renders (context value changes behave like parent state), or (3) its context subscription fires. Every 'component doesn't update' bug is one of: the setter received the SAME reference (mutation), the change happened outside React's knowledge (direct DOM edit), or the update DID happen but a memoized child legitimately skipped re-rendering (memo comparison true — the fix is stabilizing or restructuring props).

The Profiler discipline (the tool separation): DevTools 'Highlight updates when components render' shows WHO re-renders and how often; the Profiler records commits with per-component durations AND the cause ('state hook 1 changed'). This converts 'my app feels slow' into a named component with a named reason. The disciplined follow-ups: why-did-you-render in dev logs the exact prop/state difference per render — the tool that ends memo-guessing.

The production generalizations (senior-level close): log render triggers to catch event-driven re-render storms (a context value changing every keystroke re-rendering the whole tree — fix: split contexts, memoize the value); use Error Boundaries to make render-crashes recoverable and reported with component stacks; and treat key misuse as a first-class debugging suspect — duplicate or index keys produce 'wrong row updates when I edit' symptoms that look like state bugs but are identity bugs. The summary that lands: 90% of React 'bugs' are reference-identity or dependency-contract violations — check those two first.
